models_evaluated: ICOVAI (ResUNet-a segmentation + random forest CO-RADS classifier)

links.outcome: Performance on internal test versus independent external multicenter validation (CO-RADS kappa, lung opacity DSC)
links.effect: CO-RADS linear weighted kappa fell from 0.78 internal to 0.62 external (p<0.0001); opacity segmentation fell from DSC 0.76 to mDSC 0.59 (p<0.0001); lung contour unchanged (0.97).
links.quote: External validation can highlight the shortcomings of a predictive model, which were not apparent during internal testing on CT scans sampled out of the same cohort.

links.outcome: Performance drop when applied to data from other institutions than development
links.effect: Significant reduction in lung opacity segmentation (DSC 0.76 to 0.59) and CO-RADS agreement (kappa 0.78 to 0.62) on external multicenter data.
links.quote: Our work shows that published results of COVID-19 segmentation on internal test sets may not generalize well to patient data from other institutions.

links.outcome: Independent external validation versus internal testing by developers
links.effect: Independent validation revealed significantly lower performance (kappa 0.62 vs 0.78; opacity DSC 0.59 vs 0.76), showing that internal results overstated performance.
links.quote: The study demonstrates the importance of independent external validation of AI models.

links.outcome: Performance across sites in external multicenter validation
links.effect: External multicenter validation (five hospitals) showed reduced performance versus internal test; annotation platform differences and site variation may contribute. Site-specific results not reported.
links.quote: We observed a significant reduction in performance on the external test as compared to the internal test for lung opacity segmentation and CO-RADS prediction, but not for lung contour segmentation.

openai.country: The Netherlands; Belgium; France; Singapore; United Kingdom; Italy
openai.sample_unit: CT scans in final external validation analysis

links.outcome: Independent external validation versus internal testing
links.effect: CO-RADS weighted kappa fell from 0.78 internally to 0.62 externally (p < 0.0001).
links.quote: For CO-RADS classification, agreement with radiologists on the internal set was substantial (kappa = 0.78), but significantly lower on the external set (kappa = 0.62, p < 0.0001).

links.effect: Lung opacities DSC was 0.59 on external validation versus 0.76 internally (p < 0.0001).
links.quote: Lung opacities segmentation performance was adequate internally (DSC = 0.76), but significantly worse on external validation (DSC = 0.59, p < 0.0001).

links.outcome: external vs internal segmentation and CO-RADS classification performance
links.effect: Internal vs external: lung opacity DSC was 0.76 vs 0.59 (p < 0.0001); CO-RADS linear kappa was 0.78 vs 0.62 (p < 0.0001); lung contour DSC was 0.97 in both (p = 0.97).
links.quote: Lung opacities segmentation performance was adequate internally (DSC = 0.76), but significantly worse on external validation (DSC = 0.59, p < 0.0001).
